source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen, Texas campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity, second among the 19 Texas data centers that publish power figures and about 16 percent of the 475 MW published statewide.

Capacity disclosure in Texas is the exception, not the rule. The state is mapped to 133 data center sites, and fewer than one in seven publish a power figure, so the 475 MW state total is a floor rather than a census. The same caution applies here: 77 MW is what the operator states, not what the grid has agreed to serve.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 77 MW is roughly 1,900 racks of compute, housed across three co-located buildings, DFW3, DFW4 and DFW5, and 976,000 square feet of technical space in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro. The certifications on the campus, HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and SSAE 16 Type II, describe regulated healthcare, federal and payment workloads. Large-scale AI training carries no standard compliance requirement, so those qualifications narrow rather than broaden the campus's likely tenant base. Green Globes points to energy efficiency, which is a secondary concern when power is the binding constraint.

The record does not say whether any of this capacity serves AI workloads, whether the operator plans to expand, or where the power comes from. It carries no street address and no coordinates, so the facility is placed by city only. The suitability score of 76 rests on published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing. Read the 77 MW as a nameplate figure for a compliance-oriented campus, not as evidence of AI compute at this location.
